affected_predicate.description: The account olivia@10.0.2.2 from muted_accounts.csv is imported into the @test@10.0.2.2 account's muted list with the file's hide-notifications setting applied.

competing_trace_defects.description: After reaching Mastodon Settings, the trace performs a static scroll and leaves without opening the visible @test@10.0.2.2 account settings, abandoning a relevant navigation path.
The trace repeatedly treats profile-screen controls as possible settings entry points after they visibly open profile-sharing or handle-information UI, producing unrelated repeated interactions.

chains.rationale: At the reuse target, the prediction explicitly follows the reused account-name attempt as a failed premise and navigates back, visibly exiting Mastodon to the launcher and creating an off-track detour. The trace later corrects that navigation defect by reopening Mastodon, selecting Home, using the Home-screen settings control, and entering @test account settings, so the target-linked mechanism is recovered and interrupted. Later screens inspect Filters and Privacy and reach, but none exposes whether olivia@10.0.2.2 was imported or whether the hide-notifications setting was applied.

summary: The sole strict-MHR reuse creates a temporary off-track exit from Mastodon after preserving the account-name navigation premise. That mechanism is later corrected through the Home-screen settings path. The terminal screens do not expose whether the CSV account was imported. Independent prefix defects are the early abandonment of the initially reached Settings screen and the repeated profile-sharing navigation loop.
